blends.description: A refined, lighter blend perfect for traditional afternoon tea service.
blends.flavor_profile: Light, refreshing, aromatic, refined without being too strong
blends.history: Lighter blend designed for afternoon tea service (4pm). Meant to accompany delicate sandwiches and pastries without overwhelming refined flavors.
blends.popular_brands: Fortnum and Mason, Twinings, Harney and Sons
blends.serving_suggestions: Without milk for purists, or light milk. Pairs with cucumber sandwiches, scones, petit fours.

blends.description: A Western interpretation of chai, designed for latte-style preparation with a sweeter profile.
blends.flavor_profile: Sweet-spicy, creamy when prepared with milk, vanilla undertones
blends.history: Popularized by coffee shops in the 1990s as a sweeter, more accessible version of traditional masala chai.
blends.ingredients: Black tea, cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, cloves, vanilla, sometimes honey powder
blends.popular_brands: Starbucks, Tazo, Oregon Chai, David's Tea, Teavana
blends.serving_suggestions: Mix with steamed milk and sweetener, can add vanilla syrup, popular as both hot and iced latte

blends.description: A festive blend that captures the spirit of the holidays.
blends.history: Traditional holiday blend, especially popular in Scandinavia. Each family may have their own recipe.
blends.ingredients: Black tea, cinnamon, orange peel, cloves, almonds, sometimes vanilla
blends.popular_brands: Harney & Sons, Fortnum & Mason, Nordic brands
blends.serving_suggestions: Perfect with holiday cookies, gingerbread, pairs with Christmas desserts

blends.description: Liver-supportive blend with traditional cleansing herbs.
blends.health_benefits: Traditional liver support herbs, digestive bitters, gentle cleansing
blends.history: Modern blend combining traditional liver-supportive herbs. Bitter flavor stimulates digestion.
blends.ingredients: Dandelion root, burdock root, milk thistle, ginger, lemon peel
blends.serving_suggestions: Drink between meals. Course of 2-4 weeks traditionally.

blends.base_tea: Yerba mate or green tea base
blends.description: Natural energy blend with yerba mate and green tea.
blends.health_benefits: Natural sustained energy, adaptogenic ginseng, mental clarity
blends.history: Natural energy alternative to energy drinks. Combines multiple caffeine sources with adaptogens.
blends.ingredients: Yerba mate, green tea, ginseng, guarana, peppermint, citrus peel
blends.serving_suggestions: Morning or early afternoon. Avoid before bed.

blends.appearance: Cloudy green with rice pieces visible
blends.aroma: Toasted rice, green tea, enhanced umami
blends.description: Enhanced genmaicha with matcha powder adding extra nutrition and umami.
blends.flavor_profile: Toasty, nutty from rice with umami boost from matcha, satisfying and complex
blends.health_benefits: Balanced caffeine, digestive benefits, matcha antioxidants, fiber from rice
blends.history: Traditional genmaicha enhanced with matcha powder. The matcha adds color, nutrition, and umami depth. Popular for everyday drinking.
blends.ingredients: Green tea, roasted brown rice, puffed rice, matcha powder
blends.popular_brands: Ito En, Yamamotoyama, Japanese specialty brands
blends.serving_suggestions: Good for everyday drinking, pairs with Japanese food, naturally sweet enough without sugar.

blends.description: The strongest of the breakfast blends - robust Assam designed for Irish preference.
blends.flavor_profile: Very strong, malty, robust, designed to stand up to milk
blends.history: Irish tea culture favors very strong, malty blends. Ireland has one of the highest per-capita tea consumption rates. Barry's and Lyons dominate the market.
blends.ingredients: Predominantly Assam with some Ceylon or African
blends.serving_suggestions: Always with milk and sugar. Multiple cups throughout the day is the Irish way.

blends.appearance: Medium brown with blue cornflower petals
blends.aroma: Delicate bergamot with sweet citrus and floral hints
blends.description: A gentler, more floral interpretation of Earl Grey with additional citrus elements.
blends.flavor_profile: Lighter, more floral than Earl Grey with citrus notes
blends.health_benefits: Similar to Earl Grey, with additional vitamin C from citrus peels
blends.history: Created by Twinings in the 1990s as a lighter alternative to Earl Grey. Named to complement the Earl Grey name.
blends.ingredients: Black tea, bergamot oil, lemon peel, orange peel, cornflower petals
blends.serving_suggestions: Delightful on its own or with light sweetener, excellent iced

blends.description: A tropical escape in a cup, popular for both hot and iced tea.
blends.health_benefits: Vitamin A and C from mango, antioxidants from tea
blends.history: Developed to capture tropical fruit flavors in tea form.
blends.ingredients: Tea base, mango pieces, natural mango flavoring, calendula petals
blends.serving_suggestions: Excellent iced with coconut milk, pairs with tropical fruits or Thai cuisine

blends.description: Oolong tea enhanced with fragrant osmanthus flowers for sweet, fruity perfume.
blends.flavor_profile: Sweet apricot-like osmanthus perfume with oolong complexity
blends.health_benefits: Aromatherapy benefits, antioxidant oolong, traditional digestive aid
blends.history: Osmanthus (sweet olive) flowers bloom in autumn and have been used to scent tea for centuries. The fragrance suggests apricot and peach.
blends.ingredients: Oolong tea scented with osmanthus flowers
blends.serving_suggestions: Excellent afternoon tea. Good for multiple steeps. No additions needed.

blends.appearance: Reddish amber with rose petal pieces
blends.description: Classic Chinese black tea scented with rose petals for romantic floral character.
blends.flavor_profile: Romantic rose perfume with smooth black tea base, floral and comforting
blends.health_benefits: Rose calming aromatherapy, black tea antioxidants, traditional beauty benefits
blends.history: Traditional Chinese scented tea. Rose has been used to scent tea for centuries. The floral character complements rather than masks the black tea base.
blends.ingredients: Black tea scented with rose petals
blends.popular_brands: Harney and Sons, TWG, Chinese specialty brands
blends.serving_suggestions: Lovely for afternoon tea. Can take light milk. Pairs with floral desserts.

blends.appearance: Pale green, sometimes with pink petals
blends.aroma: Cherry blossom, subtle salt, green tea
blends.description: Japanese green tea with salted cherry blossoms for spring celebration.
blends.flavor_profile: Delicate cherry blossom with subtle salt and green tea base
blends.health_benefits: Green tea antioxidants, seasonal celebration, mindfulness benefits
blends.history: Spring seasonal tea celebrating cherry blossom season (hanami). The salt-preserved cherry blossoms are a traditional Japanese preparation that intensifies the floral character.
blends.ingredients: Sencha or gyokuro, salted cherry blossoms, cherry leaf
blends.serving_suggestions: Pairs with Japanese spring sweets. Seasonal and celebratory.

blends.description: A sweet, fruity blend perfect for those who enjoy berry flavors.
blends.history: Created as part of the flavored tea boom in the late 20th century.
blends.ingredients: Black tea, strawberry pieces, strawberry leaves, natural strawberry flavor
blends.serving_suggestions: Excellent iced, can add vanilla or cream, pairs with scones or fruit tarts

blends.description: Soothing demulcent blend for throat and voice support.
blends.health_benefits: Demulcent herbs soothe throat, traditional voice support
blends.history: Developed by Traditional Medicinals founder Rosemary Gladstar. Used by professional singers. Clinically studied formula.
blends.ingredients: Licorice root, slippery elm bark, marshmallow root, wild cherry bark
blends.serving_suggestions: Steep covered to retain volatiles. Drink 3-6 cups daily when needed.

companies.description: Online-focused tea retailer with extensive selection. Known for sampler programs and custom blending platform.
100% family-owned 3 generations, Charleston Tea Garden (only American tea garden)
World's first producer-owned tea brand, 3000+ products in 111 countries
Family-owned American tea company founded by John Harney. Known for quality and wide selection. Popular for flavored and classic teas.
World's #1 tea company, 400M daily consumers, 110+ countries
UK's leading tea brand, pioneered pyramid tea bags in 1996
Australian tea brand known for bold flavors and colorful packaging. Acquired by Unilever in 2013.
1000+ tea varieties, 70+ boutiques in 42+ countries, 24-karat gold flakes
Major Indian tea brand, one of largest family-owned tea businesses. Known for chai and everyday black teas.
One of world's oldest tea companies, founded in 1690. Pioneered gyokuro production. Traditional Japanese teas.

cultivars.characteristics: Natural sweetness, delicate, vivid green color
cultivars.name: Asahi
cultivars.notes: Rare, difficult to cultivate, highly prized for matcha

cultivars.common_uses: Black tea, specialty green tea for health
cultivars.name: Benifuuki
cultivars.notes: Originally for black tea, now studied for allergy relief

cultivars.name: Da Bai
cultivars.notes: Big White cultivar, prized for white tea production

cultivars.name: Jin Xuan (TTES #12)
cultivars.notes: Developed by Taiwan Tea Research Station, released 1981. Named after grandmother

cultivars.name: Longjing #43
cultivars.notes: Developed for West Lake Longjing, accounts for 80% of production

cultivars.characteristics: High quality China type, good muscatel, cold tolerant
cultivars.name: P312 Darjeeling
cultivars.notes: Popular Darjeeling cultivar known for producing excellent muscatel flavor.

cultivars.characteristics: Complex flavor, traditional Taiwan oolong cultivar
cultivars.common_uses: High Mountain Oolong, Dong Ding, Baozhong, Oriental Beauty
cultivars.name: Qing Xin (Green Heart)
cultivars.notes: Original Taiwan oolong cultivar, brought from Fujian 200+ years ago

cultivars.name: Ruan Zhi
cultivars.notes: Literally 'Soft Stem', easier to process than Qing Xin

cultivars.characteristics: Ancient bushes, complex mineral character, heavy roast capable
cultivars.name: Shuixian Old Bush
cultivars.notes: Old growth Shui Xian with enhanced complexity from age.

cultivars.characteristics: High quality, good for high elevation, refined flavor
cultivars.name: TRI 2025
cultivars.notes: Developed by Sri Lanka Tea Research Institute. Premium cultivar for high elevation.

cultivars.characteristics: Extremely early budding, tender, delicate character
cultivars.name: Wuniuzao
cultivars.notes: One of earliest budding cultivars, prized for first spring teas.

families.characteristics: Tropical trees and shrubs, aromatic, large flowers
families.notes: The custard apple family - tropical medicinal plants

families.common_uses: Flowers used for anti-inflammatory and immune support
families.notes: The daisy family - note allergy potential for ragweed-sensitive individuals

families.characteristics: Climbing/trailing vines, tendrils, separate male/female flowers
families.notes: The gourd family - includes medicinal vines

families.common_uses: Unique nutritional profile due to nitrogen fixation
families.notes: The legume family - rooibos is endemic to South Africa

families.notes: Small tropical family - Moringa is most important medicinally
Traditionally used for nervous system support

families.characteristics: Buckwheat/Knotweed family - herbs with swollen nodes
families.common_uses: Yellow dock, rhubarb root, buckwheat tea
families.notes: Many species with medicinal roots. Includes edible buckwheat.

families.characteristics: Willow family - trees and shrubs, often near water
families.common_uses: White willow bark (pain relief - natural aspirin source)
families.notes: Source of salicin which inspired development of aspirin.

families.common_uses: Lemon verbena, blue vervain, relaxation teas
families.notes: Many aromatic species used in traditional medicine and flavoring.

herb_regions.description: Immense plant diversity; indigenous medicine; conservation concerns
herb_regions.name: Amazon Rainforest

herb_regions.description: ENDEMIC region for rooibos - UNESCO biodiversity hotspot; EU PDO status since 2021
herb_regions.name: Cederberg Region

herb_regions.description: Ancient cultivation site; high-quality herbs; export-oriented
herb_regions.name: Nile Delta

herb_regions.description: Valley of Roses produces premium rose products; annual Rose Festival
herb_regions.name: Rose Valley

makers.description: Specializes in single-herb teas rather than blends. Pharmacy/health food channel.
One of America's largest herbal tea brands. Known for creative flavors and distinctive artwork on boxes.
makers.notable_products: Sleepytime, Tension Tamer, Bengal Spice, Red Zinger

makers.description: Founded by Master Tea Blender John Harney; family-owned; extensive loose leaf selection
makers.notable_products: Hot Cinnamon Spice, Paris, Dragon Pearl Jasmine, 300+ varieties

makers.certifications: B Corp (founding member), Fair Trade, Climate Neutral, USDA Organic
makers.description: Founded by brother-sister team; emphasis on art and tea; strong sustainability focus
makers.notable_products: 130+ organic ingredients from 30+ countries; Holistic Herb Teas, Flowering Teas

makers.description: British herbal tea company with Ayurvedic influence. Strong organic and ethical sourcing commitment.
makers.notable_products: Night Time, Three Ginger, Love, Turmeric Gold

makers.description: Large bulk herb supplier. Wide selection of organic and conventional herbs.
Major British tea brand with growing herbal selection.
makers.notable_products: Super Fruits, Super Green, Pure Infusions

makers.description: Historic tea company (since 1706) with extensive herbal range alongside traditional teas.

regions.climate: Subtropical highland, misty, significant day-night temperature variation
regions.description: Most famous Taiwan high mountain tea region. Misty conditions, bamboo forests. Produces exceptional light oolongs with creamy, floral character.
regions.name: Alishan

regions.description: Korea's largest tea-producing region, beautiful tea terraces. Known for high-quality pan-fired green teas.
regions.name: Boseong

regions.description: Northern Thailand, Chiang Rai Province. Settled by Chinese KMT refugees who brought tea cultivation.
regions.name: Doi Mae Salong

regions.description: Anhui province sacred mountain. Misty conditions create exceptional teas. Multiple famous varieties from different elevations and processing.
regions.name: Huangshan (Yellow Mountain)

regions.climate: Tropical highland with two rainy seasons
regions.description: World's largest tea exporter, 3rd largest producer. High elevation (4,000-9,000 ft). Year-round production. Mainly CTC processing.
regions.name: Kenya

regions.description: Blue Mountains of South India. Year-round production possible. Fragrant, aromatic teas with citrus notes.
regions.name: Nilgiri

regions.description: Black Sea coast. Turkey's main tea region. 5th largest tea producer globally.
regions.name: Rize Province

regions.description: Ali Shan, Li Shan, Da Yu Ling - premium oolongs from extreme elevations
regions.name: Taiwan High Mountains

regions.description: Home of ancient tea trees and birthplace of tea cultivation
regions.name: Yunnan Province

teas.appearance: Dark amber liquor, brownish aged leaves
teas.flavor_profile: Rich, sweet, medicinal, dates, honey, complex, smooth
teas.health_benefits: Traditional Chinese medicine uses, digestive aid, transformation creates unique compounds, "one year tea, three years medicine, seven years treasure"
teas.history: White tea aged 10-30+ years develops dramatically. Transforms from fresh/floral to rich/sweet/medicinal. Highly prized in China. Appreciation growing globally. Like fine wine aging. Properly stored in cool, dry conditions. Becomes smoother, more complex. Pharmaceutical-like properties develop.
teas.name: Aged White Tea (10+ years)
teas.processing: Aged Gong Mei or Shou Mei, stored 10+ years

teas.appearance: Pale green-white leaves, nearly clear liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Delicate, sweet, fresh, amino acid richness, minimal astringency
teas.health_benefits: Extremely high amino acids (especially theanine), antioxidants, calming energy
teas.history: Named 'white tea' because leaves appear white during early spring growth due to rare genetic mutation. Actually a green tea (pan-fired). Very high amino acid content. Prized variety rediscovered in 1980s.
teas.name: Anji Bai Cha (Anji White Tea)

teas.appearance: Varies by producer
teas.flavor_profile: Clean, unique Australian terroir, developing character
teas.health_benefits: Local production, reduced food miles
teas.history: Small but growing Australian tea industry. Daintree and other regions producing. Focus on quality over quantity.
teas.name: Australian Grown Tea

teas.appearance: Pale leaves (lighter than typical yancha), light amber liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Delicate floral, honey, fresh, unique pale color for yancha
teas.health_benefits: Antioxidants, gentler than heavily roasted yancha
teas.history: One of Wuyi "Four Famous Bushes" alongside Da Hong Pao. Legend says monks discovered pale leaves. Very rare. Lighter processing than most yancha. Delicate, not heavily roasted.
teas.name: Bai Ji Guan (White Cockscomb)

teas.appearance: Larger brownish-green leaves, pale yellow liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Mild, earthy, slightly nutty, lower quality than Sencha
teas.health_benefits: Very low caffeine, gentle on stomach, everyday tea
teas.history: Harvested after Sencha (summer/autumn). Uses larger, more mature leaves. Lower grade but popular daily tea in Japan. Very affordable. Sometimes roasted to make Hojicha.
teas.name: Bancha
teas.processing: Steamed, made from later/larger leaves and stems

teas.appearance: Golden-brown tips, pale amber liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Sweet, honey, malt, subtle fruit
teas.health_benefits: Antioxidants, gentle caffeine, immune support
teas.history: Premium Ceylon white tea from high-elevation estates. Unique golden color distinguishes it from Chinese white teas.
teas.name: Ceylon Silver Tips

teas.appearance: Large leaves with abundant golden tips, bright orange-red liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Honey, sweet, malty, fruity, sweet potato, chocolate, pepper, hazelnut
teas.health_benefits: Antioxidants, naturally sweet (low bitterness), gentle energy
teas.history: Created 1939 during WWII when transport routes from Fujian were cut. Uses large-leaf Yunnan assamica variety (same as pu-erh). More golden tips = higher quality. Jin Ya (Golden Bud) is pure tips. Smooth, naturally sweet, little astringency.
teas.name: Dian Hong (Yunnan Gold)

teas.appearance: Tightly spiraled green leaves with white downy fuzz, pale green liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Fruity, floral, delicate, sweet, peach, apricot
teas.health_benefits: High antioxidants, supports immune system, gentle energy
teas.history: One of China's top 10 famous teas. Requires 13,000-15,000 shoots per kilogram. Intercropped with fruit trees (peach, plum, apricot), creating natural fruity notes. Harvest window is only 15-20 days in early spring.
teas.name: Dong Ting Bi Luo Chun (Green Snail Spring)

teas.appearance: Dark twisted leaves with some golden tips, deep red-brown liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Bold malty character, caramel, dried fruit, robust yet smooth
teas.health_benefits: Energizing, rich in polyphenols, supports metabolism, warming
teas.history: Fengqing County is considered the birthplace of Yunnan black tea. The region's ancient tea trees and expertise in processing create exceptional quality.
teas.name: Fengqing Dian Hong

teas.appearance: Twisted dark leaves, bright amber liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Smooth, honey notes, light malt, unique Caucasian terroir
teas.health_benefits: Unique terroir antioxidants, gentle stimulation
teas.history: Tea production began in Georgia 1840s. Once major Soviet producer. Now rebuilding specialty reputation with heirloom cultivars.
teas.name: Georgian Black Tea

teas.appearance: Green-gold rolled leaves with golden flower pieces, golden liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Sweet osmanthus fragrance, apricot, peach, floral elegance
teas.health_benefits: Calming aromatic properties, aids digestion, antioxidant, traditional use for skin health
teas.history: Oolong tea scented with dried osmanthus flowers (gui hua), which bloom in autumn. The sweet olive fragrance complements the tea's floral notes. A popular choice in Chinese restaurants.
teas.name: Gui Hua Oolong (Osmanthus Oolong)
teas.processing: Light-medium oxidation, scented with dried osmanthus flowers

teas.appearance: Tightly rolled emerald-green balls, pale golden liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Floral, orchid, buttery, creamy, sweet, clean, complex
teas.health_benefits: High antioxidants, L-theanine (promotes calm alertness), supports mental clarity, gentle energy
teas.history: Cool high-altitude temperatures (often below 18°C/64°F) and frequent fog slow leaf growth, concentrating flavor compounds and creating sweeter, more complex flavor. Da Yu Ling (2,600m) is highest, rarest, most expensive.
teas.name: High Mountain Oolong (Gao Shan)
teas.origin: Taiwan - Ali Shan, Li Shan, Da Yu Ling (1,000-2,600m elevation)
teas.processing: Lightly oxidized, hand-rolled into tight balls

teas.appearance: Small yellow-green leaves, yellow liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Sweet, mellow, slightly nutty
teas.health_benefits: Gentle energy, digestive support, antioxidants
teas.history: Historic yellow tea from Anhui province. Rare production. Yellow tea processing creates mellow, sweet flavor without green tea's grassiness.
teas.name: Huo Shan Huang Ya (Yellow Buds)

teas.appearance: Pure golden buds, bright golden-orange liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Honey, fruity, sweet, smooth, chocolate, longan fruit, no astringency
teas.health_benefits: High antioxidants, smooth energy, gentle on stomach
teas.history: Created 2005 in Tongmu village (same area as Lapsang Souchong). Requires 50,000-60,000 buds per 500g. Extremely expensive premium tea. Sweet, fruity, smooth, zero bitterness. Revolutionary modern Chinese black tea.
teas.name: Jin Jun Mei (Golden Eyebrow)
teas.processing: Orthodox processing, made only from golden buds
teas.steep_time: 2-3 minutes (very quick due to bud tenderness)

teas.appearance: Fine leaves with some tips, golden-amber liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Muscatel, floral, delicate sweetness, Darjeeling-like but distinctly Nepali
teas.health_benefits: High antioxidants from high altitude, supports vitality, gentle energy
teas.history: Jun Chiyabari is a pioneering Nepali estate producing exceptional teas rivaling top Darjeeling. Small-lot artisanal production with extraordinary attention to quality.
teas.name: Jun Chiyabari (Nepal First Flush)

teas.appearance: Dark leaves, deep copper-red liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Full-bodied, strong, slightly harsh, powerful
teas.health_benefits: Antioxidants, high energy
teas.history: Historic region where James Taylor established Ceylon's first commercial tea estate in 1867 at Loolecondera. Mid-elevation teas. Strong, full-bodied character.
teas.name: Kandy
teas.origin: Sri Lanka - Kandy district (2,000-4,000 ft mid-elevation)

teas.appearance: Purple-tinged leaves, reddish-purple liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Smooth, mellow, slightly sweet, minimal astringency
teas.health_benefits: High anthocyanins (antioxidants that give purple color), may support cardiovascular health, unique polyphenol profile
teas.history: Developed from rare purple-leaf mutation discovered in Assam. Contains anthocyanins (like blueberries). Launched commercially 2011. Grown at high altitude (6,000-8,500 ft). Lower caffeine than regular tea. Unique health properties.
teas.name: Kenyan Purple Tea

teas.appearance: Medium-sized leaves, bright green liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Balanced sweetness and vegetal notes, nutty undertones, accessible refinement
teas.health_benefits: Good antioxidant content, supports focus, gentle stimulation
teas.history: Harvested in late May to early June. Jungjak offers a balance between the premium early harvests and everyday later pickings.
teas.name: Korean Jungjak (Third Picking)

teas.appearance: Large sun-dried leaves, pale golden-green liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Wild, forest character, mineral, unique ancient tree depth
teas.health_benefits: Wild tea rich in diverse compounds, supports vitality
teas.history: Remote Phongsali province has ancient tea trees related to Yunnans. Local ethnic minorities have harvested wild tea for centuries. Growing specialty interest.
teas.name: Laos Ancient Tree Green

teas.appearance: White pearls that unfurl, golden liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Sweet, honey, malt, fruity, smooth
teas.health_benefits: Antioxidants, gentle energy
teas.history: Malawi produces excellent handcrafted white teas. Zomba Plateau (6,000 ft elevation). Hand-rolled into pearls. Introduced by Satemwa Estate. Unique African white tea.
teas.name: Malawi Zomba Pearls

teas.appearance: Long dark twisted leaves, golden liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Intense honey orchid aroma, sweet, floral, complex, peachy
teas.health_benefits: High antioxidants, energizing
teas.history: Most famous Dan Cong variety. Intensely aromatic natural honey-orchid scent. No flavoring added - all natural. Can be overwhelming if oversteeped. Very popular internationally.
teas.name: Mi Lan Xiang Dan Cong (Honey Orchid)

teas.appearance: Silver-white buds and young leaves, pale golden liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Sweet, floral, honey, delicate, clean
teas.health_benefits: High antioxidants, gentle energy, mountain minerals
teas.history: Nepal produces exceptional high-altitude white teas (5,000-7,000 ft). Ilam region borders Darjeeling. Similar terroir. Clean, pure mountain character. Shangri-La brand represents Nepali premium whites.
teas.name: Nepali Shangri-La

teas.appearance: Yellowish-green buds, bright yellow liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Sweet, mellow, subtle corn notes, gentle vegetal, smooth finish
teas.health_benefits: Very gentle on stomach, aids digestion, calming, antioxidant-rich
teas.history: A lesser-known yellow tea from Zhejiang. Huang Tang means yellow soup referring to the distinctively yellow liquor. Production is rare and mostly local.
teas.name: Pingyang Huang Tang (Yellow Soup)

teas.appearance: Large silvery leaves with characteristic antler shape, pale golden liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Floral, honey, stone fruit, African terroir character, delicate sweetness
teas.health_benefits: Very high in antioxidants, gentle caffeine, supports immune health
teas.history: Produced by Satemwa Estate in Malawi, one of Africa's oldest tea estates. The unique antler-shaped leaf presentation creates a striking appearance. African white tea with exceptional quality.
teas.name: Satemwa Antlers (Malawi White)

teas.appearance: Compressed cakes (bing), tuo, brick; golden-green (young) to dark amber-brown (aged) liquor
teas.aroma: Fresh and vegetal (young) or deep, complex, earthy-sweet (aged)
teas.caffeine_level: Medium-High (60-80mg per cup for young, less for aged)
teas.flavor_profile: Bright, vegetal, floral, fruity (young) transforming to dried fruits, plum, camphor, leather, tobacco (aged 10-30+ years)
teas.health_benefits: Supports digestion, may aid weight management, complex antioxidants (age-dependent), microbial benefits from aging
teas.history: Designed for long-term aging (15-50+ years optimal). Transforms dramatically with proper storage (humidity 60-70%, temp 20-28°C). Young sheng can be very astringent. Ancient tree (gushu) material is most prized. Major mountains: Bulang, Yiwu, Bada, Ban Zhang.
teas.name: Sheng Pu-erh (Raw)
teas.origin: China - Yunnan Province (various mountains: Bulang, Yiwu, etc.)
teas.oxidation: Varies with age (minimal when young, complex when aged)
teas.processing: Sun-dried maocha, naturally aged or stored young

teas.appearance: Long twisted dark leaves, orange-amber liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Floral, orchid, mineral, roasted, fruity, complex
teas.health_benefits: Antioxidants, digestive support, warming
teas.history: One of Wuyi's traditional teas. Lao Cong (old bush, 50+ years) is especially prized. Also grown in Phoenix Mountain as Dan Cong style. Versatile cultivar with floral character.
teas.name: Shui Xian (Narcissus/Water Sprite)
teas.origin: China - Wuyi Mountains, Fujian (also Phoenix Mountain)
teas.processing: Moderately oxidized, roasted, yancha or Dan Cong style

teas.appearance: Dark twisted leaves, deep reddish-brown liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Full-bodied, earthy undertones, robust, hint of tobacco
teas.health_benefits: Strong antioxidants, energizing, warming properties
teas.history: Sumatra tea estates, established in colonial era, produce robust teas. Less known than Java but developing specialty reputation.
teas.name: Sumatra Black Tea

teas.appearance: Flat, unrolled dark green leaf fragments, bright green liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Rich umami, sweet, vegetal, complex depth
teas.health_benefits: Extremely high in L-theanine and chlorophyll, powerful antioxidant, calm alertness
teas.history: The raw material for matcha. Shaded growing increases chlorophyll and L-theanine dramatically. Rarely sold as leaf tea - almost all is stone-ground into matcha. Drinking tencha as leaf tea is a special experience.
teas.name: Tencha
teas.processing: Shade-grown (20+ days), steamed, dried without rolling

teas.appearance: Small dark leaves, dark reddish-brown liquor
teas.flavor_profile: Robust, bold, slightly astringent, full-bodied, classic Turkish character
teas.health_benefits: Strong antioxidants, very energizing, supports alertness
teas.history: Turkey is one of the worlds largest tea producers and consumers. Rize province on the Black Sea coast produces virtually all Turkish tea. Traditionally brewed strong in a double teapot (çaydanlik).
teas.name: Turkish Organic Rize (Çay)

teas.appearance: Fine yellowish leaves, golden-yellow liquor
